title: Funnel trumpet
summary: The Kamba funnel trumpet is a bamboo trumpet of the Akamba, fitted into a calabash funnel as a resonator and played by young men for amusement. A metre-long bamboo tube stopped at the upper end is blown across a rectangular notch, with the calabash funnel at the bottom amplifying the sound.
howToPlay: Four notes of the trumpet are lit along the tube, the higher ones nearer the notch.
A band of breath runs from the notch to the note you strike, and rings of sound leave the funnel.
Long notes swell slowly: strike close to the beat and let them ring.
rules: A call is a line of long notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It is a young players' instrument, played for amusement rather than at public events.
credits: Tradition: the Kamba funnel trumpet; phrases written for this game
